title: If Listening, as I Listen Still
description: If Listening, as I Listen Still in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 465 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Help thou my unbelief."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: If lis-tening, as I lis-ten still, O God! to thine in-struc-tive word, In spite of all my spi-rit's will, Some whis-pering voice of doubt is heard, That voice spon-ta-neous from the soul, Which nought can check and nought con-trol;

lines: If listening, as I listen still,
O God! to thine instructive word,
In spite of all my spirit's will,
Some whispering voice of doubt is heard, —
That voice spontaneous from the soul,
Which nought can check and nought control;
If when most earnestly I pray
For light, for aid, for strength from thee,
Some struggling thoughts will force their way,
If reason, thy best gift, will hold
Hath many a word of mystery;
I read not all thy record yet,
But teach me, Lord! and none shall be
More prompt, more pleased to learn of thee.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
